rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the one who purifies himself and that person's reward, the passage turns to the one who corrupts himself and his wretched fate.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر المزكي وثمرته ،   أتبعه المدسي وشقوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miser withholds what God commanded or encouraged him to give; he seeks independence from people and from promised reward, trusting deluded hopes, so he neither benefits people nor works for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فمنع ما أمر به وندب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He denies al-ḥusnā, bringing about denial of what deserves to be affirmed and believed.
rows.anchor: أي أوقع التكذيب أن يستحق التصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the denier is fixed on sensible things like livestock, God prepares him for the most difficult, most adverse course.
rows.anchor: ولما كان جامداً مع المحسوسات كالبهائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿusrā is the hardest and most distressing trait: doing what angers God, which leads to Hell and to its causes.
rows.anchor: أي للخصلة التي هي أعسر الأشياء وأنكدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majestic plural used for both paths signals how remote taking either path is: good is ringed by hardship, while reason and original nature restrain evil.
rows.anchor: وأشار بنون العظمة في كل من نجد الخير ونجد الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matter was settled in eternity through the designation of the blessed and the wretched; the author invokes the Prophetic saying that each person is facilitated toward what he was created for.
rows.anchor: وذلك كله أمر قد فرغ منه في الأزل بتعيين أهل السعادة وأهل الشقاوة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says that each person is facilitated toward what he was created for; the author cites this as a summary of the preceding decree.
rows.anchor: وكل كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم - ميسر لما خلق له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of this world escape crises with money, but the wealth this miser withheld in hope of benefit will not help him in that hour.
rows.anchor: أهل الدنيا إذا وقعوا في ورطة تخلصوا منها بأموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be read as an interrogative denial, which negates the wealth's usefulness with greater force.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون استفهاماً إنكارياً فيكون نافياً للإغناء على أبلغ وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taraddā means perishing by falling into the grave's pit and Hell; the root conveys destruction and falling into a well.
rows.anchor: أي هلك بالسقوط في حفرة القبر والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In reply to an obstinate person's question about why God does not guide everyone to good, God distinguishes what He graciously undertakes from what He does by sovereign power; no one has a right over Him.
rows.anchor: ما له لا ييسر الكل للحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God has undertaken is to make the true path clear and establish evident proofs of it.
rows.anchor: البيان للطريق الحق وإقامة الأدلة الواضحة على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After guidance might sound like an obligation on God, this verse asserts His complete dominion over both worlds: the person who rejects guidance harms only himself, and God grants or withholds as He wills.
rows.anchor: فمن ترك ما بينا له من طريق الهداية لم يخرج عن كونه لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase addresses the deniers and asserts that the afterlife and this world belong exclusively to God.
rows.anchor: أي يا أيها المنكرون خاصاً بنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order gives priority to the afterlife because the deniers need that emphasis, not for rhyme; he rejects arranging revelation solely for rhyme, citing the end of al-Tawba and noting that alternative wordings could also rhyme.
rows.anchor: وليس التقديم لأجل الفاصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic restriction continues the repeated distinction between the abodes of the virtuous and the wicked, denying that they are treated alike.
rows.anchor: تخصيص كل من المحسن والمسيء بداره بطريق الحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched is the unbeliever, who undergoes Hell's heat continuously; a sinful believer may enter it, but not in that abiding manner.
rows.anchor: فإن الفاسق وإن دخلها لا يكون ذلك له على طريق اللزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever corrupts his knowing faculty by denying what should be affirmed, and his acting faculty by arrogantly and stubbornly turning from truth, refusing to give wealth to purify himself.
rows.anchor: أفسد قوته العلمية بأن أوقع التكذيب بما حقه التصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future particle conveys assuredness with respite, while the passive construction suggests that separating the God-fearing person from Hell is effortless.
rows.anchor: بما أفهمته السين من التأكيد مع التنفيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-atqā is the person whose knowing faculty is firmly established and who reaches the highest degree of piety by avoiding idolatry and sins.
rows.anchor: فكان في الذروة من رتبة التقوى وهو الذي اتقى الشرك والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction is consistent with the earlier verse: a sinful believer may enter Hell and later leave, whereas the most wretched unbeliever is its abiding occupant.
rows.anchor: فإن الفاسق يدخلها ثم يخرج منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He spends his wealth on good purposes, thereby cleansing and developing himself, avoiding base traits and adopting good ones; this contrasts with denial and turning away.
rows.anchor: أي يصرفه في مصارف الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ḥatbāk: mentioning denial first implies omission of its opposite second, while mentioning giving wealth second implies omission of its opposite first.
rows.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر التكذيب أولاً دليلاً على حذف ضده ثانياً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the previous sūra's promise to the pious, the oath comforts the Prophet, the most pious: revelation's pause was a trial, though he brings good for religion, this world, and the afterlife; day and night sustain human life and much of its hereafter.
rows.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أتقى الخلق مطلقاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḍuḥā is the sun's rising brightness, the day's most noble, gentle, and luminous span; its expansive light suits the highest-ranked creation, and Abu Bakr is intended first among the pious.
rows.anchor: فذكر ما هو أشرف النهار وألطفه وهو زهرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After promising to raise the Prophet continually in rank and honor, God recalls the care with which He had already raised him.
rows.anchor: وعده بأنه لا يزال في كل لحظة يرقيه في مراقي العلا والشرف

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: The Prophet's father died while he was still a fetus and his mother when he was eight; being fully orphaned before puberty meant no created person had a claim over him, as Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says.
rows.anchor: يكون عليه - كما قال جعفر الصادق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God found him orphaned and took him into care.
rows.anchor: أي يصادفك أي يفعل بك فعل من صادف آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ḍāll means not yet knowing revealed laws, not actual religious deviation: the Prophet had never followed his people's religion; lack of knowledge is called by its consequence, and the verse 42:52 confirms he had not known scripture or faith.
rows.anchor: لأنه لم يكن على دين قومه في حين من الأحيان أصلاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usual chain is orphanhood, a caregiver's neglect, and consequent ignorance; thus the verse names the result, misguidance, for its cause, lack of knowledge.
rows.anchor: يلزم من اليتم في الغالب عدم العلم لليتيم لتهاون الكافل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before revelation, sound reason and original nature had already led him to monotheism and related truths; he refrained from actions whose rulings he did not know, and this sound nature is a form of piety.
rows.anchor: إلا ما علمت بالعقل الصحيح والفطرة السليمة المستقيمة من التوحيد وبعض توابعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God then gave him comprehensive guidance, teaching what he had not known through revelation, inspiration, and enabling him to reason correctly.
rows.anchor: فعلمك بالوحي والإلهام والتوفيق للنظر ما لم تكن تعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀʾilan can mean burdened with dependents whom he could not afford to support generously, or simply poor.
rows.anchor: ذا عيال لا تقدر على التوسعة عليهم أو فقيراً

rows.speaker: ابن القطاع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ distinguishes the verbs: ʿāla a man means he became poor, while aʿāla means he had many dependents.
rows.anchor: قال ابن القطاع : عال الرجل : افتقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enriched him first through commercial profit and later through the gains of war; this suggests four human conditions: possessing both religion and worldly means, neither, religion alone, or worldly means alone.
rows.anchor: بما جعل لك من ربح التجارة ثم من كسب الغنائم وقد أفهم ذلك أن الناس أربعة أقسام

words: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ فِىٓ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human kind gathers wondrous created features that demonstrate the Creator's knowledge and power and includes many believers; Abraham, their father, is twice associated with the holy land, Jerusalem and Mecca, preparing for the response to the oath.
rows.anchor: جامعاً لبدائع المصنوعات التي هي لما ذكر من حكمها دالة على كمال علم خالقها وتمام قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means that God determined and brought the human species into existence by His overwhelming greatness and might.
rows.anchor: أي قدرنا وأوجدنا بما لنا من العظمة الباهرة والعزة الغالبة القاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human species combines desire and intellect and self-familiarity that can distract a person from important concerns.
rows.anchor: هذا النوع الذي جمع فيه الشهوة والعقل وفيه الأنس بنفسه ما ينسيه أكثر مهمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' question about creating one who will corrupt and shed blood reflects their awareness that anger and desire combined with intellect produce conflict, corruption from desire, and bloodshed from anger.
rows.anchor: لأنهم علموا أنه إذا جمع الغضب والشهوة إلى العقل جاءت المنازعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Best stature encompasses spirit and intellect, or more broadly the whole human: upright posture, beauty, sensory capacities suited to life's purpose, and a gathering of qualities found across created beings; thus man is called the microcosm.
rows.anchor: بما جعلنا له من حسن الخلق والخلق بما خص به من انتصاب القامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God endowed humans with an original, sound nature, unchanged in its first disposition and prepared to receive truth.
rows.anchor: الفطرة الأولى التي لا تبديل لها من الطبع الأول السليم الذي هيأناه به

rows.speaker: الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Al-Aṣfahānī likewise explains the verse about people being one community through the original human disposition.
rows.anchor: على الفطرة الأولى قال الأصفهاني

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Barrajān says the human is naturally formed upon Islam, the upright religion.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن برجان هنا : مفطور على فطرة الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With reason, God enables people to rise from Hell's depths to the gardens through faith and excellent deeds; prophets, especially Muhammad, and his learned, wise, luminous followers show this human potential.
rows.anchor: منحناه عقلاً يهديه إلى العروج عن درك النيران إلى درج الجنان بالإيمان والأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī describes the human as tall, eating with his hand, and adorned with reason and discernment.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : خلقه سبحانه وتعالى مديد القامة يتناول مأكوله بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason is humanity's true purpose and is called its lubb, or core; the author connects the core purpose of things with divine law, as discussed at the end of al-Nisāʾ.
rows.anchor: والعقل هو المقصود في الحقيقة من الإنسان لأن من أسمائه اللب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human intellects are broadly comparable, but innate dispositions vary: temperament can undermine reason, while people may be astute in one subject and dull in another; these differences organize human livelihoods and crafts.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن عقول الناس بحسب الخلق متقاربة

rows.speaker: الأستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī argues that God is transcendent above composition and form: if He had a shared attribute such as form, He would be the best instance of it, since the Creator surpasses creation in shared attributes.
rows.anchor: قاله الأستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري في تفسيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim attributed to some elders that nothing more excellent than the existing world is possible; levels can vary without limit, as human forms and colors already show.
rows.anchor: وصيغة  "  أفعل  "  لا تدل على ما قاله الزنادقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, best may be relative to something God wills us to recognize; Sunni doctrine, stated by al-Ashʿarī and al-Ghazālī, holds that God's possible acts are limitless.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن تكون صيغة أفعل مفيدة بالنسبة إلى شيء أراده الله بحيث إن نتفطن له نحن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī identifies the philosophers' denial of God's will and claim that He acts by necessity as the source of their error; he affirms God's power over every possible thing.
rows.anchor: وبين أن هذا من قواعدهم لنفيهم صفة الإرادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible thing is whatever God can bring about; impossibility means affirming a thing while denying it, or affirming a specific or two while denying its general category or one. Thus a more excellent world is possible, and God can create other worlds of different sizes.
rows.anchor: وعرف أن الممكن هو المقدور عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence recalls the commands to recount God's favor and seek Him in the previous sūra, then the demonstration of His power and wisdom in al-Tīn, which establishes resurrection and the need to prepare for judgment.
rows.anchor: أمره سبحانه وتعالى في الضحى بالتحديث بنعمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra answers how believers may earn a good recompense and stand before the supreme King on the great gathering day: it guides them to the traits of faith and righteous action.
rows.anchor: فتشوف السامع إلى ما يوجب حسن الجزاء في ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening introduces foundational knowledge by recalling man's creation and some of his good and bad states, prompting wonder at God's power and reflection on His signs.
rows.anchor: فقال بادئاً بالتعريف بالعلم الأصلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is placed before its prepositional phrase for greater impact, especially as this was the first revelation and reading was the urgent command; its object is omitted to indicate that the reading commanded is the Qurʾān, comprehensive of all good.
rows.anchor: وقدم الفعل العامل في الجار والمجرور هنا لأنه أوقع في النفس لكونها أول ما نزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading in the Lord's name may mean beginning with the basmala, seeking help from the beneficent Lord, or mentioning His name; on the last reading, the name stands for His sublime attributes.
rows.anchor: حال كونك مفتتحاً القراءة { باسم ربك } أي بأن تبسمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentators say this indicates that recitation is not complete without invoking God's name; honoring the name honors its bearer and all that is attributed to Him.
rows.anchor: قالوا : وهذا يدل على أن القراءة لا تكون تامة إلا بالتسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than the all-encompassing Greatest Name, the verse uses the nurturing Lord's attribute, gathering the other attributes and comforting the Prophet as the first revelation came while he loved solitude in worship at Ḥirāʾ.
rows.anchor: ولكونه في سياق الأمر بالطاعة الداعي إليها تذكر النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: While the Prophet was devoted to solitude at Ḥirāʾ, Gabriel came with the first five verses of this sūra, ending with the phrase about what he did not know.
rows.anchor: فجاءه جبرائيل عليه الصلاة والسلام بخمس آيات من أول هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening functions like a longer, more reassuring basmala: it alludes to the Greatest Name through the full set of perfect attributes, universal mercy through creation, and particular mercy through honor and teaching that guides to divine approval.
rows.anchor: ولهذا السر ساقه مساق البسملة بعبارة هي أكثر تأنيساً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to recite also alludes to seeking refuge from devils, as the Qurʾān interposes a hidden barrier and God commands refuge before recitation.
rows.anchor: وأشار إلى الاستعاذة بالأمر بالقرآن لما أفهمه قوله سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is named before command because it is perceptible, easier to conceive, and clearer evidence of God's existence, power, and wisdom; knowing God through His acts is the first obligation.
rows.anchor: وبدأ بالخلق لأنه محسوس بالعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object makes creation universal: God determines and brings every existent thing into being, and each remains subject to His permission, prevention, harm, and benefit.
rows.anchor: وحذف مفعوله إشارة إلى أنه له هذا الوصف وهو التقدير والإيجاد على وفق التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are singled out because man is the highest animal and the essence of its kind, gathers the qualities of the cosmos, and is especially wondrous to create, proving the Maker's perfection and exclusive right to worship.
rows.anchor: وكان الإنسان أكمل الحيوان وزبدة مخضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān here is the human species, characterized by familiarity with itself, its sensed traits, and the people of its own kind.
rows.anchor: أي هذا الجنس الذي من شأنه الأنس بنفسه وما رأى من أخلاقه وحسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blood is the origin of humans and other animals and the substance of life; God forbade eating it because it imparts its own nature to the eater.
rows.anchor: وكان الله تعالى قد حرمه لأنه أصل الإنسان وغيره من الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God built this world on causal processes and wisdom, although He can create directly without a chain of causes.
rows.anchor: بنى هذه الدار على حكمة الأسباب مع قدرته على الإيجاد من غير تطوير في تسبيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlaq is the plural of ʿalaqa, a thick, dark-red clotted blood; the same term also names mud that sticks to the hand.
rows.anchor: وهو دم شديد الحمرة جامد غليظ

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī uses this verse as evidence that a shared term may be applied to both of its meanings at once, since human creation is associated with both blood and sticky earth.
rows.anchor: فالآية من أدلة إمامنا الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه على استعمال المشترك في معنييه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may also allude to the prohibition of eating our original substances, blood and earth, before transformation; once they transform, they may become lawful, since transformation affects legal status in marriage and other matters.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى حرمة أكل ما هو أصلنا من الدم والتراب قبل أن يستحيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A red emission of semen is not a transformation, since it was already red before desire reduced it; sometimes desire is too weak to condense it and it is emitted red.
rows.anchor: واحمرار النطفة ليس استحالة ؛ لأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blood that transforms into flesh takes the ruling of lawful flesh, as earth mixed with water and transformed into dates or grain becomes lawful.
rows.anchor: فإذا تحول الدم لحماً صار إلى جنس ما يحل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the question about what could make the Prophet disbelieve in judgment cannot imply his own doubt; its intended audience is his community, who may hesitate despite clear evidence.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير : لما قال الله سبحانه وتعالى لنبيه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr compares the address to conditional warnings such as the threat that associating partners would void one's works: its wording can extend to the Prophet, while its actual concern is the community, who are not protected from error.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr argues that, since God is the wisest judge, differences among people after their creation in the best form cannot be purposeless; creation is not vain.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects the placement of al-ʿAlaq after al-Tīn to the Qurʾān as the remedy that explains beginnings and ends; recitation and reflection clarify the way, and the Qurʾān is guidance, mercy, and good news.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links humanity's creation in the best form and return to the lowest state to divergence in people's destinies and views, all according to prior wisdom and will; God could have given every soul its guidance.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the two preceding sūras describe the highest human destiny, the Prophet's promised satisfaction and the excellence of his state, surpassing even Moses' prayer for an expanded breast.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Al-ʿAlaq then points to the other end of the human spectrum, from the one who forbids a servant to pray through the command not to obey him, contrasting the two ranks.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Answering the objection that al-ʿAlaq was among the earliest revelations, Ibn al-Zubayr says sūra order follows the Prophet's arrangement, whether divinely instructed or based on the Companions' judgment, not chronology.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
